- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +3–5% above true value); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 periods after spike.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above true value, reduce next forecast by 1–3% to align with recent mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; dampen forecast sensitivity to sentiment >0.8 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +1.3, -1.2, +1.1), model often misaligns with true trend; use sentiment average as a smoothing filter for next forecast.
